data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Genuine reliability is distinguished from mere compliance by the presence of 'Negative Constraint Validation'\u2014the ability of the panel to reject a correct outcome based on a checklist failure.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist is so tightly coupled to the outcome that no 'independent' negative constraints exist.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel is incentivized only by the final outcome rather than process adherence.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If a panel is merely tracking the right answer (compliance), they will subconsciously 'force' the checklist items to be 'Yes' when the outcome is known to be positive. Genuine reliability is proven when the panel identifies a 'False' on a checklist item even when the final outcome is 'Correct', or when they correctly identify 'decoy' failure modes (negative constraints) that do not actually affect the outcome but test the rigor of the process.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
